title: Uber Unleashes Robotaxis in Europe, Beginning a Cautious Rollout in Croatia
summary: Uber has officially launched its first autonomous vehicle (AV) ride-hailing service in Europe, choosing Croatia's capital, Zagreb, as its initial proving ground. Operated in partnership with Chinese AV firm Pony.ai, the service allows riders to book self-driving electric vehicles through the Uber app, with a human safety driver always on board.
content:
The future of urban transport just took a significant stride onto European soil. Uber has officially launched its first autonomous vehicle (AV) ride-hailing service on the continent, commencing operations this week in the Croatian capital, Zagreb.

Beginning Wednesday, riders in Zagreb can now hail a self-driving car directly through the familiar Uber app. This groundbreaking European debut is a collaborative effort with Chinese autonomous driving technology firm Pony.ai, marking a strategic expansion for both companies. Crucially, and perhaps reassuringly for early adopters, every autonomous ride will still feature a human safety driver behind the wheel, ready to intervene if necessary.

This pilot program leverages electric vehicles, positioning the service not just at the forefront of autonomy but also within the growing e-mobility trend. The choice of Zagreb as the European launchpad is strategic; while larger markets often present more complex regulatory hurdles, cities like Zagreb can offer a more agile environment for initial trials and data collection.

For Uber, this move signifies its continued commitment to integrating AV technology into its global network, following deployments in parts of the United States and other regions. While fully driverless operations remain a future aspiration for many, these carefully managed launches with safety drivers are vital steps, allowing the technology to mature, gather real-world data, and build public trust. The road ahead for autonomous vehicles in Europe is long, but with Zagreb now on the map, Uber has truly begun to chart its course.
keyTakeaways: Uber has launched its first autonomous vehicle (AV) ride-hailing service in Europe, starting in Zagreb, Croatia.
The service operates in partnership with Chinese firm Pony.ai and includes a mandatory human safety driver.
This marks a cautious but significant step for AV expansion in Europe, utilizing electric vehicles for initial trials.
author: Darius Popa
